Thank you for letting us know about the leak at Lot 4, Craigieburn Rise.

As the source of the leak is your dishwasher — an appliance within your private lot — the repair and any resulting damage to your flooring are the responsibility of the lot owner rather than the owners corporation. The owners corporation is not in a position to send a plumber on your behalf for a private-lot matter.

2. Arrange a licensed plumber to repair the leak as soon as possible.
3. Contact your home and contents insurer, as the floor swelling may be claimable under your policy.

If the leak is found to have affected any common property or another lot, please notify us straight away so we can assess whether the owners corporation needs to take any action.

Kind regards,
Fictional Strata Partners Pty Ltd

Dear Owner of Lot 103,

Thank you for your email regarding the dog in Lot 12, and we apologise that this matter has not been resolved to your satisfaction despite being raised previously.

The rules for Elara Residences are clear on this point. Rule 5.2 (Animals on common property) requires that dogs be on a lead at all times on common property, and that owners immediately remove and dispose of any animal waste. Rule 2.1 also requires that common property not be used in a way that unreasonably interferes with other residents' use and enjoyment of it. The conduct you have described — an off-lead dog in the lobby and waste left by the lift — is a breach of both rules.

As this is a repeat matter, we will refer it to the committee for a decision on the appropriate next steps, which may include issuing a formal breach notice to the occupant of Lot 12. We will keep you informed of the outcome.

We appreciate your patience and thank you for continuing to raise these concerns.

Kind regards,
Fictional Strata Partners Pty Ltd
Owners Corporation Manager — Elara Residences (PS612884K)
rows.reasoning: The complaint directly engages Rule 5.2 (dogs on lead, waste removal) and Rule 2.1 (unreasonable interference with common property). This is a repeat complaint, making it priority rather than routine. Deciding whether to issue a formal breach notice to Lot 12 is an enforcement decision that belongs to the committee, so requires_committee_decision is true.
